statement: What is the units digit of $9^{2027} + 4^{2026}$?

choices.misconception: I thought every power of 9 ends in 9 and every power of 4 ends in 4, so I added 9 + 4 = 13.
I multiplied the two units digits, $9 \times 6 = 54$, instead of adding them.
I thought odd powers of 9 end in 1, and then added 1 + 6.
I found the units digit of $9^{2027}$ and forgot to add $4^{2026}$.

hints: Write out the units digits of the first few powers of 9 and of 4.
Only units digits affect the units digit of a sum. Powers of 9 and powers of 4 each have a short repeating pattern of units digits, so decide where 2027 and 2026 fall in their patterns.
Powers of 9 end in 9, 1, 9, 1, ... and powers of 4 end in 4, 6, 4, 6, ...

solutions.reliable: The powers 9, 81, 729, ... end in 9, 1, 9, 1, so odd powers of 9 end in 9, and $9^{2027}$ ends in 9. The powers 4, 16, 64, 256, ... end in 4, 6, 4, 6, so even powers of 4 end in 6, and $4^{2026}$ ends in 6. The sum ends like $9 + 6 = 15$, so its units digit is 5. The transferable idea: units digits of powers repeat in short cycles, so a huge exponent only matters through its place in the cycle.

whyOnTest: Last-digit questions test that units digits of powers cycle; a huge exponent only matters through its place in the cycle, here odd or even.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
